grade_reason: Grade A. U = 0: every rate is published by Sydney Water, the fixed charges accrue daily over a stated quarter, GST-free rests on Commonwealth statute, and the applicable usage rate is settled by a dated observation from the storage authority. The trigger mechanics remain open and cannot change the number at 92% storage.

reference_connection.designation: Sydney Water publishes one metered residential water service charge, A$26.65 a quarter, without differentiating by meter size; the unmetered charge is a separate and higher figure for a different customer.

billing_note: Fixed charges are billed quarterly but accrue daily, and a quarter is 90, 91 or 92 days. The published figures use the longest quarter, which is why the charge is annualised by days from the declared year length rather than multiplied by four.

cases.label: Sydney Water typical quarterly house bill, 50 kL over 92 days
cases.detail: 26.65 water service + 50 x 3.41 usage + 189.88 wastewater service = 387.03. Computed at the non-drought rate, which is what the publisher's own typical figure uses.

public_reconciliation.note: The reconciliation also settles a structural question: the publisher's typical bundle is water service, water usage and wastewater service, and excludes stormwater.

component_states.basis: A supply of water is GST-free by statute, s 38-285. The backflow test fees on the same Sydney Water page are quoted as including GST, which is consistent: a testing service is not a supply of water.

component_states.resolution: Resolved 17 August 2026. Greater Sydney storage is 92%, published by WaterNSW. The drought rate engages below 60%, so the normal rate applies.

component_states.question: The exact retail trigger mechanics are still not established: WaterNSW's wholesale determination defines a 31-day lag at Part 7 Clause 25 and Sydney Water's retail page states the thresholds without one. Material only near a crossing. At 92%, 32 points above the engagement threshold and moving 0.1 point a week, no lag of any length selects the drought rate — so the number does not depend on the answer and this is a validation gap rather than a blocker.
component_states.reverts_to_material_when: Greater Sydney storage approaches 60%. The reclassification is a property of this state, not of the question.

components.name: Drinking water usage
components.rate_display: A$3.41/kL in the normal state; A$3.84/kL while the drought state is engaged

excluded.reason: A$30.26 a quarter for a house, A$9.67 for a unit, and only in declared drainage areas. Varies by dwelling type and location, is excluded from universal comparison under §8, and is not part of the publisher's own typical bundle.

Apply only to properties with a testable backflow prevention device, which Sydney Water states are not typical houses. The test fees are also GST-inclusive, being a service rather than a supply of water.

excluded.item: Sydney Olympic Park recycled water charges
excluded.reason: Provided by the Sydney Olympic Park Authority and collected by Sydney Water on its behalf. A different supplier and a locality-specific service.

excluded.item: Pension rebate on fixed service charges
excluded.reason: Rule 3.1: means-tested, describes a subset of households, and is not universal or automatic.

scope_disclosures: Reference account is a separately metered residential property. An unmetered property pays A$181.56 a quarter instead and is a different reference customer.

The wastewater service charge is a fixed amount that Sydney Water states already contains a deemed amount for usage. Sydney's total water services figure therefore does not vary with the volume of water used, which is unusual in this Index and is the reason it is comparable at all — unlike Perth, where sewerage rests on a property valuation.
The published rate is the non-drought rate. The drought rate applies while Greater Sydney storage sits below the 60/70 trigger, and the state has not been captured.
shape_note: A flat volumetric rate with two daily-accrued fixed charges. The 92-day quarter is annualised from the declared year length of 365.2425 days, not by assuming four quarters make a year: 365.2425/92 = 3.9700 quarters, so A$26.65 a quarter is A$105.79 a year rather than A$106.60.

tariff_state.rule: Greater Sydney storage below 60% engages the drought usage rate; it disengages above 70%.
tariff_state.structural_note: A drought rate is part of the tariff architecture, not a discretionary relief measure: an existing regulatory rule fires on a measured condition. It therefore moves the structural price and the index, unlike Tokyo's basic-charge waiver which moves only the payable price.
tariff_state.trigger_provenance_note: The trigger is taken from Sydney Water's own retail pricing page and nowhere else. WaterNSW's wholesale determination defines a 31-day lag at Part 7 Clause 25; the thresholds look identical, which is why borrowing it here would be invisible in the output and wrong.
tariff_state.resolution_note: The rule comes from Sydney Water's retail page and the state from WaterNSW, which is the storage authority. Rule and state together make the applicable rate: A$3.41/kL, the normal state.

jurisdiction.note: City is a display layer. The observation belongs to jurisdiction x utility x service area x customer class x schedule x period.
